notes.text: I'm going to call get_mission first to pull up the mission details.

I'm laying out the problem first: six unknowns, and each test drop can reveal the impact point, the fall time, whether it lands in the smoke, and the wind at aircraft altitude. I'm weighing drops at several altitudes, since those would read the wind directly at each height, with fall time shaped by drag and the relative wind. I'm also planning to keep the test drops within 500 m of the origin and to start with a drop aimed at the smoke column.

I'm settling on a first drop at altitude 100 m, heading 90 and speed 60, released from (-200, 0), well away from the smoke so it reads pure wind.

I'm working out the wind at 100 m, which blows toward about 206°, roughly south-southwest at 10.7 m/s. The impact displacement comes to about +50.9 east and -53.1 north from the release point, and the fall takes 7.19 s. Since the no-drag fall time would be only about 4.52 s, the longer fall suggests drag is involved, or the release altitude is lower than I assumed.

Quadratic drag would slow the vertical fall as well, so a 7.19 s fall points to a terminal velocity of roughly 15 to 20 m/s. Horizontally, the load starts at 60 m/s east while the air moves only about 4.7 m/s east and 9.6 m/s south, so the drag acts on a large relative velocity and should cut the load's eastward speed quickly. I'm trying to see how a net 50.9 m eastward drift fits with that.

I'm estimating the drag coefficient from the horizontal deceleration: a relative speed of about 65 m/s would require k around 0.05 to 0.08 to bring the load's eastward speed down within a second or two. That gives a terminal velocity near 11 m/s, which is roughly consistent with the 7.19 s fall. Rather than solving this by hand, I'll test hypotheses with the compare tool, since each call checks all the test drops at once.

I'm planning the remaining nine drops: one at 30 m to measure wind shear, one at 150 m for the wind there, and a few released inside the smoke at (0,0) to detect an updraft from the entered-smoke flag and impact shift. I also want some drops at different speeds and headings so I can pin down the drag.

I'm planning the next drop so I can pin down how strongly the drag depends on aircraft speed.
